metadata.note: The Wilmington and Northern: Wilmington, Delaware up the Brandywine to Coatesville, the Hay Creek valley to Birdsboro and the Schuylkill's west bank to Reading (about 73 mi). Built as the Wilmington and Reading (Delaware and Pennsylvania State Line + Berks and Chester, consolidated 1866), which ran trains 1869-1876; reorganized after foreclosure as the Wilmington and Northern (1877); leased 999 years to the Philadelphia and Reading from 1 Feb 1900 (Reading Company from 1924). Rule 4: each of the three main-line pieces is one feature per operator, sharing geometry (W&R, W&N, Reading). The Reading era reuses the existing 'Philadelphia and Reading Railroad / Reading Company' string and colour (read programmatically from reading_main_line.geojson and others). Branches drawn: French Creek (1888 anchor), Delaware River Extension (1883 and 1889 anchors), plus the Octoraro Railway's dated 1984 excursion.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. Probed old_railway_operator for 'Wilmington and Northern', 'W&N', 'Wilmington & Northern' and 'Reading', and note:old_railway_operator: no way carries a W&N or W&R spelling in any old_railway_operator key; the road is tagged old_railway_operator=Reading with the name 'Wilmington and Northern Branch' (active East Penn Railroad / Brandywine Valley Railway track, Elsmere Jct - Coatesville), 'Delaware River Extension' and 'St. Peters Branch'. opstrace's Operator match was extended to read note:old_railway_operator, name and plain operator (research/notes/osm-plain-operator-key-lifted-grades.md), and railway=abandoned/razed/demolished ways were fetched separately (research/notes/opstrace-drops-railway-demolished.md).

OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) railway ways for the lifted Coatesville - Birdsboro grade, the French Creek Branch and the Wilmington approach. Geometry only: OHM dates are not used for any segment (research/notes/openhistoricalmap-geometry-source.md).

Waypoints: Nominatim, each type checked. Montchanin, Guyencourt, Granogue, Lenape, Wawaset, Northbrook, Embreeville, Mortonville, Wagontown, Brandamore, Icedale, Suplee, Joanna, Geigertown (hamlets), Chadds Ford, Pocopson, Warwick (villages); Modena, Coatesville, Elverson, Birdsboro and Reading returned 'administrative' boroughs/city (centroids checked against the line: all within 0.5 km). Hand-pinned: the Wilmington PW&B junction and the 1869 loop south of Elsmere, Gibraltar and a west-bank point below it (Nominatim's Gibraltar is a hamlet node off the track; Robeson returned the township and was not used), High's Jct, South Reading, the Reading P&R depot, St. Peters (end of the OHM branch) and Pigeon Point (Nominatim returned a road). Simplified Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals; despike left on (no known hairpin on this road; per-station mileposts checked, see each geometry_quality).
not_yet_sourced: Reading-era passenger END on every section: Wilmington-Coatesville drawn to 1915 [OPEN], Coatesville-Birdsboro and Birdsboro-Reading to 1901 [OPEN]. Upper bound Sept 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide daggers); the only dated end is a Birdsboro marker's '1949'. Needs Reading public timetables 1920s-1940s, PUC/PSC discontinuance orders or a 'last train' story.
W&R Coatesville-Birdsboro START drawn from 1874 [OPEN start]: the June 1870 opening may or may not have carried passengers.
Wilmington terminal history: PW&B 1877, French Street 1881, PRR King Street 1915 (Fowler), B&O Water Street (Harwood 2002, undated) - only the PW&B/PRR approach is drawn.
Birdsboro-Reading routing after 1901: the W&N west-bank line or the Reading main line via Exeter.
French Creek Branch passenger span beyond the 1888 anchor, including any Reading-era service (block [11], omitted).
Delaware River Extension: years of boat-train/park service beyond the 1883 and 1889 anchors.
Octoraro Railway excursions 1977-1994 other than 7 Jul 1984.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.
branches_deliberately_omitted: [3] Wilmington and Reading: Birdsboro - Reading (High's Jct extension) - drawable NONE: no source places a W&R passenger train into Reading.
[11] Philadelphia and Reading: French Creek Branch (Reading era) - drawable NONE: no 1901t or 1915t letter, no other source.
[14] Delaware River and Lancaster: Kimberton - St. Peters - drawable NONE: no source says passenger trains ran.
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn, as freight/industrial spurs with no passenger listing: Rockland, Kentmere/Rising Sun, Hagley, Christiana Avenue, South Walnut Street, Water Street, Mill Creek and wharf branches, the Sankanac quarry wye, the Reading Belt Line use of Birdsboro-High's Jct after 1901, and all Conrail/Octoraro/Brandywine Valley/East Penn freight years except the dated 1984 excursion (Rule 1).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 32.8 mi drawn against 33.2 mi documented (Wikipedia W&N Branch route diagram, Wilmington 0.0 - Coatesville 33.2). Elsmere Jct-Coatesville follows the surviving Wilmington and Northern Branch (OSM name 'Wilmington and Northern Branch', operator East Penn Railroad / Brandywine Valley Railway, old_railway_operator=Reading); the Wilmington end follows OpenHistoricalMap's ways dated 1869-12-24 (the W&R's original line: the loop south of Elsmere and the run north-east beside the PW&B) - geometry only, OHM dates not used. Per-station check against the route diagram's mileposts: Montchanin 7.3/7.3, Granogue 11.2/11.4, Lenape 19.1/19.1, Embreeville 25.9/26.0, Modena 30.9/31.0 (each station within 0.2 km of the line). The line stops at the junction with the PW&B about 0.45 mi short of the Wilmington (PW&B, later PRR King Street/French Street) station; trains ran that last stretch over PW&B/PRR track, which is not drawn in this company's colour. LATER/OTHER ALIGNMENT CAVEAT: from 1881 the W&N had its own approach to a French Street terminal in Wilmington, and Harwood (2002) puts Reading-era trains at the B&O Water Street station; neither approach is drawn - every era here is drawn on the 1869 approach to the PW&B, which is right for 1869-1880 and for the 1915 PRR terminal but not for whatever years used French Street or Water Street. North of Elsmere the drawn track is the modern freight alignment; no realignment there is recorded in the report.

segments.note: Wilmington and Reading Railroad (Delaware and Pennsylvania State Line + Berks and Chester, consolidated 1866). First section opened: a special passenger train ran Coatesville - Wilmington on 24 Dec 1869 (Mansley 1996 via Wikipedia) and regular service is in the 1870 Official Guide (Fowler: 'Modeville 1870G' = Modena, 'Harvey's 1870G'); Fowler 'y' (1875G) at Mortonville, Lenape and Chadd's Ford. Trains used the PW&B into Wilmington. In receivership 1875-76 but still the W&R; sold at foreclosure 4 Dec 1876, so 1876 is this operator's last year. Headway 360 min is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1869 start from Wikipedia (Mansley 1996, special train 24 Dec 1869) and Fowler's 1870G entries; 1876 end is the foreclosure sale (ICC 1931 valuation p.603 via Wikipedia). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Wilmington and Reading Railroad through the Hay Creek valley to Birdsboro (ore and iron traffic for the Brooke works). START IS OPEN: Wikipedia says the line to Birdsboro 'opened June 22, 1870', but the Birdsboro station article says only 'a freight line'; the first PASSENGER evidence is Fowler's 'Liggett's 1874G' (Cedar Knoll) in the 1874 Official Guide, with Joanna, Conestoga, Suplee and Birdsboro 'y' (1875G). 1874 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known opening - passenger service may have begun as early as 1870. Do not move the start earlier without a passenger source. Ends 1876 with the foreclosure. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1874 start from Fowler table 141 ('Liggett's 1874G'); 1875G letters at Joanna, Suplee, Birdsboro; 1876 end from the foreclosure (Wikipedia). The 1870 opening conflict (Wikipedia W&N vs Birdsboro station article) is recorded, not resolved. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Wilmington and Northern Railroad, the new company formed after the W&R foreclosure (Feb-Apr 1877); its 1877 annual report lists 11 passenger and baggage cars and arranges use of the PW&B station in Wilmington. Extended to French Street, Wilmington, in 1881 (Fowler DE table 45 'Wilmington (French Street) z' = 1888t; city stops Silverbrook, Newport Road, Sixth Avenue and Madison Street all 'z'). Henry A. du Pont president from 1879. The P&R bought control in 1898 but the W&N ran its own trains until the 999-year lease to the Philadelphia and Reading took effect 1 Feb 1900, so 1899 is this operator's last full year. Headway 240 min is an estimate, not counted from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1877 start from the reorganization and 1877 annual report (Wikipedia, Google Books R30pAAAAYAAJ); service confirmed by Fowler's z (1888t) at essentially every station; 1899 end from the 1 Feb 1900 P&R lease. Headway not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 9.3 mi drawn against about 9.8-10.2 mi documented (Fowler table 141, Reading-Birdsboro). West-bank line per the report's block [9]: Birdsboro - Gibraltar - High's Jct on today's Norfolk Southern Harrisburg Line (old_railway_operator=Reading, 8.9 mi of the routed path before simplification), with the parallel east-bank ex-Reading main line through Exeter (also tagged Harrisburg Line, and OHM's line there) excluded from routing by hand. About 0.8 mi runs on the immediately parallel ex-PRR Schuylkill Branch grade beside the W&N track west of Birdsboro, within about 50 m of it. High's Jct - Reading P&R depot (about 2.1 mi, untagged OSM track and a 0.1 mi connector) is APPROXIMATE: it follows surviving track from the High's Jct area north into the city to the site of the Reading P&R (Outer) depot, which the W&N reached from May 1882 by trackage rights over the Reading and Lehigh / P&R; whether this is exactly the track used, and the pre-1882 approach to the W&N's own Second and Cherry Streets station, are not established - the earlier terminal is not drawn.

segments.note: Wilmington and Northern on its own west-bank line Birdsboro - High's Jct (Robeson, Gibraltar, Seyfert, Ridgewood/Naomi), then trackage rights over the Reading and Lehigh into Reading (perpetual rights over the R&L or P&R from 1879). The 1877 annual report records a new W&N station at Second and Cherry Streets, Reading; Montgomery's History of Berks County (1886, p.895) says passenger service between Reading and Wilmington was established in 1878, so the start is 1878. From May 1882 trains ran to the P&R depot (Reading Times, 22 May 1882). Fowler 'z' (1888t) Penn Street through Clingan. The parallel Pennsylvania Schuylkill Valley (Birdsboro-Naomi, 1883) is PRR, not this line. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1878 start from Montgomery 1886 p.895 (via Wikipedia Birdsboro station); 1882 P&R depot from the Reading Times 22 May 1882 (via Wikipedia); Fowler table 141 'z' (1888t); 1899 end from the P&R lease. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Philadelphia and Reading Railway as operating lessee of the W&N from 1 Feb 1900 (Reading Company from 1924 - same railroad, not a split). Reading-era service: Fowler 'r' (1901t) at Elsmere Junction and Maryland Avenue; Fowler 'a' (1915t) at 'Wilmington (King Street) (PRR)', so W&N trains then used the PRR station; the Wilmington Evening Journal of 30 Aug 1915 (p.13) reports 'a train on the Wilmington and Northern branch of the Philadelphia and Reading Railway' at Hagley with its 'passengers ... thoroughly scared'. Harwood (2002 p.48 via Wikipedia) puts passenger trains at the B&O Water Street station instead - conflict recorded, both may be true at different dates. END IS OPEN: passenger service confirmed to 1915. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped on this section. Do not extend without evidence. A Birdsboro roadside marker says W&N passenger service ended in 1949 (not specific to this section), and the Feb 1952 Official Guide daggers Granogue (and probably Montchanin) as having no passenger service, so it was gone by Sept 1951. Freight continued under Reading, Conrail, the Octoraro Railway and now East Penn - context only. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1900 start from the 1 Feb 1900 lease; 1915 last confirmed year from Fowler DE table 45 ('a' = 1915t) and the Evening Journal 30 Aug 1915 p.13; 1951 upper bound from the Feb 1952 Official Guide index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Reading Company from 1924) as W&N lessee from 1 Feb 1900. END IS OPEN: the last confirmed year for this middle section is 1901, from Fowler's 1901t 'r' letters at both ends of the road (Millmont and Trap Rock on the Reading side, Elsmere Jct in Delaware), which imply a through Reading - Wilmington service; no station between Coatesville and Birdsboro carries its own r or a letter. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped on this section. Do not extend without evidence. Bracket: 1901 to somewhere 1915-1951; a Birdsboro roadside marker (quoted on Wikipedia, in an article with chronology errors) says passenger service on the W&N ended in 1949, and the Feb 1952 Official Guide daggers Elverson, Joanna and Brandamore. Rail service Coatesville-Birdsboro ended after Hurricane Agnes in 1972; abandoned 1984, lifted 1991 - freight, context only. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1900 start from the lease; 1901 last confirmed year from Fowler table 141 'r' (1901t) at Millmont, Trap Rock and Elsmere Jct; 1949 marker and 1952 Guide daggers recorded as bracket, not drawn. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Wilmington and Northern: French Creek Branch (Elverson – St. Peters)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no running time was seen in any source (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) railway ways, traced with opstrace.py; OSM 'St. Peters Branch' remnant at St. Peters.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 5.8 mi drawn against 5.7 mi documented (Fowler table 142; Wikipedia). Entirely on OpenHistoricalMap railway ways (geometry only; the branch was lifted after 1970), ending at the OSM 'St. Peters Branch' remnant at St. Peters. Warwick lies 0.2 km from the line.

segments.note: ANCHOR YEAR: Fowler table 142 gives 'z' (1888t, a W&N timetable) at Warwick, Foxhill, Trythall, Sancanac and St. Peter's - passenger evidence for 1888 only. Service certainly ran wider than this one year both ways (the iron-ore branch 'went into service' in May 1880, and St. Peters was also a resort village), but no other passenger year is confirmed; never widen this anchor to look plausible. Possibly a mixed train. Mines closed 1928; freight past Warwick ended 15 Dec 1970 - context only. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1888 from Fowler table 142 ('z' = 1888t) at five branch stations. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Wilmington and Northern: Delaware River Extension (Pigeon Point)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no running time was seen in any source (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. OSM 'Delaware River Extension' ways and OpenHistoricalMap CC0 ways dated 1881/1882.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced: 3.4 mi drawn against about 4.25 mi documented (0.75 mi 1881 + 3.5 mi 1882, Wikipedia) of which the Pigeon Point stub was 0.9 mi. Drawn on OSM ways named 'Delaware River Extension' and OHM ways dated 1881 and 1882 (geometry only) from the W&N's 1869 line south of Elsmere, across the Christina River drawbridge, to the Pigeon Point pier. One straight-line leg: a 0.2-mi join from the main line to the start of the traced extension. The report's endpoint is Madison Street station on the W&N's city line; the extension is instead drawn from its junction with the main line, so the city end (Madison Street - Mill Creek Jct) is approximated by that junction. Hazel Dell Park and South Side Wye are not individually located.

segments.note: ANCHOR YEAR: in July 1883 the W&N 'began running trains to a pier in the Delaware River that connected directly to a steamer to Cape May' (Daily Village Record, 16 Jul 1883, via Wikipedia). Probably a seasonal boat-train service. Service may well have run in the years around 1883, but no other year is confirmed; this is a separate anchor from 1889, and the gap between them is deliberately not bridged. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1883 from the Daily Village Record 16 Jul 1883 (via Wikipedia). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: ANCHOR YEAR: a W&N timetable of 1889 lists Drawbridge Jct, South Side Wye and Hazel Dell Park (Fowler DE table 46, '1889t'; Fowler queries Drawbridge Jct as 'pass?'). The New Jersey and Wilmington Ferry Co. ran from the W&N pier to Penns Grove 1889-1917 (Baltimore Sun, 14 May 1889), but the ferry does not prove trains ran to the pier after 1889. Service certainly ran wider than this one year, but no other year is confirmed; do not widen. Mill Creek-Shellpot section abandoned 1906-1919, Pigeon Point stub 1984 - freight context only. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1889 from Fowler DE table 46 ('1889t'). Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Octoraro Railway: Elsmere Jct – Chadds Ford Jct (excursion)
properties.speed_source: estimated, not sourced: no running time was seen in any source (Rule 3)
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. Sub-section of the W&N Branch trace.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no straight-line leg: 12.0 mi, a sub-section of the Wilmington - Coatesville trace from Elsmere Jct (milepost 3.2) to the junction with the ex-PRR Octoraro Branch at Chadds Ford Jct (milepost 15.4; documented about 12.2 mi). The photographs prove the train only at Montchanin and Chadds Ford; the Elsmere Jct start is the southern end of the Octoraro Railway's lease and is not itself proven for this trip.

segments.note: ANCHOR YEAR: one dated excursion. Two Doug Lilly photographs dated 7 Jul 1984 show ex-TP&W RS-2 205 with former Reading MU cars passing the 1889 Montchanin station, and the same train at Chadds Ford as a 'mixed train excursion on the Octoraro Railway' backing onto the Brandywine bridge. The Octoraro Railway was the shortline lessee of Elsmere Jct - South Modena from 1977 to 30 Jun 1994; other excursions probably ran but their dates are not established. A charter or one-off passenger special counts under Rule 1; the Octoraro's freight years do not. Headway 1440 is a placeholder for a single trip.
sources: Segment-level: 1984 from railpictures.net photos 544039 and 568527 (both dated 7 Jul 1984).
